reason: Verified in source and in the browser at 390/768/1440. b.css .b-edit declares background: var(--back) at line 390 and re-declares background: var(--fore-06) at line 396 at identical specificity, so the computed value is rgba(255,255,255,0.06) at every width — the comment directly above ("It gets an opaque ground so nothing reads through") is contradicted by the rule it introduces. Driving master.html?v=approach&state=owner-editing, the .b-edit rect intersects other .b-item rects at all three widths: 3 rows at 1440 (Final dress fitting, Choose the evening music, Final guest numbers), 3 at 768, 4 at 390 — and with a 6% ground those rows print through the panel and over its own labels. At 390 the panel measures 154×537 because [data-medium="full"] .b-measure{padding-left:124px} outranks the @media (max-width:700px) fallback on specificity (0,2,1 vs 0,1,1), so the phone never gets the narrow lane; the title input clips (scrollWidth 174 vs clientWidth 118 on "Send the invitations"). Not covered by the gates: interaction-check.mjs opens owner-editing only at the default 1440 viewport and its only item-overlap assertion (line ~198) runs on the phone state, which has no editor. Not a constraint breach — the fix removes a colour value, adds none.
sharpenedFix: Keep the diagnosis; replace the layout mechanism, which as written is inert. (1) Delete the second background declaration on .b-edit so the opaque var(--back) stands. Do NOT add box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--fore-16) — .b-edit already carries border: 1px solid var(--fore-16), and a ring on top of it doubles the hairline and breaks the one-hairline grammar the rest of b.css keeps. If more separation is wanted once the ground is opaque, raise the existing border to var(--fore-28); nothing else. (2) padding-right on .b-measure cannot reserve a gutter: .b-item is position:absolute inside the position:relative .b-measure, so its right:0 resolves against the PADDING box and ignores padding-right. Verified empirically — setting .b-measure{padding-right:360px} at 1440 leaves .b-item width unchanged at 520px. Reserve the band on the item instead: at the existing 901px breakpoint (reuse it, do not invent 560px — at 768 the panel is still 452px wide and still covers three rows), set [data-medium="sheet"] .b-item, [data-medium="full"] .b-item { right: 376px } for the whole owner measure, not only while editing, so opening the editor never re-wraps six titles; then .b-edit { position: absolute; top: 0; right: -376px; width: 360px; margin: 0 } sits level with the item it edits and can never stand over a row. (3) Under 901px render .b-edit as position: fixed; inset: auto 0 0 0 with the input, the stepper row and the actions each on their own row, a safe-area inset-bottom pad, and the edited item scrolled clear above it; while it is open give .b-field a bottom padding equal to the sheet height so the last item is still reachable. (4) Also fix the phone lane while here: change [data-medium="sheet"] .b-measure, [data-medium="full"] .b-measure { padding-left: 124px } to sit inside @media (min-width: 701px) so the max-width:700px block actually applies at 390. (5) Assertions: run the owner-editing state at 390, 768 and 1440 and assert getComputedStyle(.b-edit).backgroundColor has alpha 1, that .b-edit's rect intersects no .b-item rect at ≥901px, that at <901px it is position:fixed and the edited .b-item's rect sits fully above it, and that the title input's scrollWidth <= clientWidth.
